To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) photochemical immobilization of 4-methyl benzoyl cellulose on silica gel has successfully been developed; (2) the resulting photochemical immobilized PMBC CSPs have been used for the chromatographic resolution of a wide range of racemic compounds and (3) the immobilization process, the cross-linking reagents and the coated amount of PMBC have been optimized in order to achieve the best chromatographic properties of the CSPs.
the immobilization process is a simple and effective way of preparing polysaccharide CSPs with improved chiral recognition ability.
photochemically immobilization of polysaccharide derivative is a promising approach for the preparation of CSPs with improved chromatographic and chiral recognition properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of chiral stationary phase based on polysaccharide materials.
the preparation of new immobilized polysaccharide stationary phases and with the investigation of the chromatographic properties.
the development of new CSPs for chiral separation by liquid chromatography, based on polysaccharide materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photochemically immobilization method provides a simple, efficient and versatile way to immobilize polysaccharide materials on silica gel.
photochemically immobilization of polysaccharide derivative on silica gel is a promising approach to produce new CSPs with improved chromatographic properties and enantioselectivity.
the immobilization of PMBC on silica gel is a promising method to obtain chiral stationary phases with high enantioselectivity and stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immobilization of PMBC on silica gel by the photochemical method is a convenient and effective procedure for the preparation of PMBC CSPs with good chromatographic and chiral properties.
the photochemically immobilization of polysaccharide CSPs is a promising method for the preparation of new chiral stationary phases with improved chiral recognition properties.
the immobilized polysaccharide materials have been found to be very efficient for the chromatographic resolution of the racemic mixtures of chiral compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemical immobilization is an effective, easy and reproducible method for preparing insoluble polysaccharide-based CSPs.
the immobilized PMBC CSPs can be used for enantiomer separations in a variety of organic solvents.
the photochemically immobilization method is very efficient and easy to apply and it is possible to obtain a very good enantioseparation using a small amount of polysaccharide derivative.
